mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on (a) Team A shots-for being below Team A shots-against AND (b) Team A shots-on-target-for being below the competition context shots-on-target mean. Measure goal output for Team A under this joint condition versus when only one or neither condition holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A goal output is further suppressed when both the shots-for deficit and the below-average on-target ratio co-occur, compared to when only one condition is present — a joint interaction rather than additive individual effects.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume is structurally low relative to the shots it concedes, and this asymmetry between shots-for and shots-against is jointly associated with a below-competition-average conversion rate (shots-on-target-for relative to shots-for). When a team produces fewer shots than it faces AND its on-target ratio is also below the competition norm, the joint condition suppresses goal output beyond what either observable alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct observables (shots and shots-on-target) for the same team and comparing their joint state against a competition-context benchmark. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For Team B, jointly track the ratio of shots-on-target-against to shots-against across the ALL_PRIOR window versus the RECENT_5 window. Test whether the recent compression of this ratio (fewer on-target shots per total shot allowed) is associated with lower goals-against in the same recent window.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's shots-on-target-against to shots-against ratio compresses in recent matches relative to its longer-run average, goals-against also falls — the joint movement of two defensive observables predicts defensive improvement beyond what either observable alone signals.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots-on-target-against has declined sharply in recent matches (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) while its shots-against has remained stable. This divergence between total shots allowed and on-target shots allowed — a within-team asymmetry across two distinct defensive observables — may indicate a structural change in defensive quality that is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint relationship between two distinct defensive observables (shots-against and shots-on-target-against) and their ratio's temporal shift, which is not reducible to a single observable's recent vs. long-run comparison.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on matches where Team A's corners-against exceeds its corners-for by a threshold margin AND Team A's possession is below its own season average. Test whether this joint condition (corner deficit + possession deficit) is associated with elevated goals-against relative to matches where only one condition holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Goals-against for Team A rises when both a corner-flow deficit and a possession deficit co-occur, more so than when either condition is present alone — indicating a non-additive joint territorial pressure effect.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A concedes substantially more corners in recent matches (RECENT_5: 7.2) than its season average (ALL_PRIOR: 4.333), while its corners-for has declined (RECENT_5: 3.2 vs ALL_PRIOR: 4.051). This simultaneous divergence in both directions — more corners conceded AND fewer corners earned — represents a joint corner-flow asymmetry that may be associated with a possession and territorial pressure shift, measurable against Team A's possession trend.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (corner_kicks and possession) simultaneously for the same team, and testing their interaction — not reducible to either observable with a single coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on matches where Team A's fouls-for is below its season average AND Team B's fouls-for is above its season average (i.e., asymmetric foul-rate regime). Test whether yellow cards and corners are elevated for Team B relative to matches where the foul asymmetry is absent or reversed.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A fouls less than its average while Team B fouls more than its average in the same match, Team B's yellow cards and corners-for rise relative to the symmetric foul-rate baseline — the asymmetric joint condition predicts a disciplinary and set-piece skew.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's foul rate has declined notably in recent matches (FOR RECENT_5: 11.6 vs ALL_PRIOR: 14.462) while Team B's fouls-against (fouls committed against them) has risen in recent matches (RECENT_5: 16.0 vs ALL_PRIOR: 15.013). This asymmetric cross-team divergence in foul rates — one team fouling less while the other is being fouled more — jointly conditions the card and set-piece environment in a way neither team's foul rate alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct observables (fouls for each team) measured asymmetrically across both sides simultaneously, then linked to a third observable (cards/corners). It is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split matches by half. For Team A, condition on whether goals-against in the second half exceed goals-against in the first half (a within-match state). Then jointly test whether elevated cards_2h (above competition context) co-occurs with this second-half goal vulnerability pattern for Team A, and whether Team B's first-half goal scoring advantage is amplified when cards_2h is elevated.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's second-half goals-against rate rises further when cards_2h is elevated above the competition context mean, and Team B's scoring advantage in the first half is more pronounced in matches where second-half card rates are high — indicating a within-match state interaction between half-level goal distribution and disciplinary escalation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Both teams show a within-match half-level goal distribution asymmetry: Team A concedes more goals in the second half than the first (AGAINST: 1H=0.41, 2H=0.667) while Team B scores more in the first half relative to the second (FOR: 1H=0.587, 2H=0.680 — nearly balanced but with a first-half lean). Jointly, the second-half card environment (cards_2h) for both teams is elevated relative to the competition context. The interaction between second-half goal vulnerability for Team A and elevated second-half card rates for both teams represents a within-match state dependency not captured by full-match averages.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires half-level resolution for goals combined with a second-half-specific card observable (cards_2h), jointly conditioning on within-match state across two distinct observables. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band, and requires half-level data resolution.
